result.summary:
Independently re-read docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-018.md in full (not TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary) and cross-checked every exact expected value it asserts against the real implementation at HEAD (b159e10), plus docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md and handoffs/WF02-REQ-018/step-02c-security-reviewer-regate.json for AC7's audit-payload shape.

Coverage check (per AC, all pass):
- AC1-AC7 each have >=1 verification case; AC-schema and AC-catalog add two mechanical checks. No AC is unaddressed. No 'TODO' anywhere in the file (grep confirmed zero matches).
- Every case names the exact route/command text, tg_id, event/user ids, SQL fixture statements, and expected reply text or DB row shape -- none rely on 'check it looks right' or an unstated judgment call.
- Every case states its failure mode ('a run where X is a FAIL').

Exact-value cross-checks against the real files (not just internal spec consistency), reading apps/bot/src/domain/{eventStaff,eventStaffAuthorization,event,auditLog}.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/{staff,checkin,venue,event}.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,en,ru}.ts, apps/bot/src/index.ts, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts, and both existing unit test files:
1. checkin.notAuthorized verbatim in en.ts: 'You are not authorized to check people in for this event.' -- matches AC1/AC3's quoted expectation exactly.
2. venue.notAuthorized / event.notAuthorized verbatim in en.ts: both 'You are not authorized to do this.' -- matches AC2 exactly, and venue.ts's makeVenueNewHandler runs checkOrganizerForChapter BEFORE validateVenueCreateInput, confirmed by reading the handler body, so AC2's dispatch is refused on authorization before field validation could matter -- the spec's claim holds regardless of the venue field values sent.
3. staff.assignmentNotificationBody (ru) verbatim in ru.ts: 'Вас назначили на встречу гостей (check-in) для мероприятия «{event}». Ваша задача на входе: поприветствовать гостя, спросить имя и подтвердить его в списке участников.' -- matches AC4's verbatim quote (with {event} substituted) character-for-character.
4. addEventStaff's payload shape {eventId, targetUserId, eventTitle} and removeEventStaff's payload shape {eventId, userId, eventTitle} (domain/eventStaff.ts §2.4) -- spec's AC5 correctly uses 'targetUserId' for the add-row check and 'userId' for the remove-row check, matching the two different field names exactly (not a copy-paste of one shape onto the other).
5. buildCheckinRefusalAudit / requireEventStaffForEvent (domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts): action 'checkin.refused', entity 'event', entityId=eventId, payload={reason}, actorUserId null iff user===null -- matches AC7a-d exactly, and matches the security-reviewer regate handoff's own live-verified values verbatim.
    isFinished (domain/event.ts:729-731) is evaluationTime.getTime() > endsAt.getTime() -- strictly-after, confirming AC3's claim that exactly-at-endsAt is still allowed.
6. writeAuditLog (domain/auditLog.ts) inserts actorUserId/action/entity/entityId/payload into schema columns actor_user_id/action/entity/entity_id/payload (db/schema.ts:310-323, actor_user_id has no .notNull()) -- matches every SQL query the spec writes against audit_log column-for-column.
7. getUserByTgUsername (domain/user.ts:131-141) does an exact eq(users.tgUsername, tgUsername) match with LIMIT 1, no case-folding -- matches design §2.2 and the spec's own stated open-question framing; not exercised with mixed case by any spec case, consistent with the design's own scope note.
8. Confirmed via git grep that no 'registration list' handler exists anywhere in apps/bot/src (`git grep -n "registration.*list|listRegistrations" apps/bot/src` -> only an unrelated schema index name, registrations_waitlist_order_idx, no handler) -- AC2's spec correctly does NOT write a case for this third named surface, consistent with the design gate's prior acceptance (design §6.5). Not a coverage gap.
9. Confirmed real exported handler names: makeVenueNewHandler (handlers/venue.ts:66) and makeEventPublishHandler (handlers/event.ts:286) -- exactly what the harness script imports; spec's own caveat ('confirm before running') is satisfied by what's actually in the file.
10. Confirmed index.ts:91-93 registers exactly three commands -- bot.command("staff_add", makeStaffAddHandler(db)), bot.command("staff_remove", makeStaffRemoveHandler(db)), bot.command("checkin", makeCheckInHandler(db)) -- matching AC-catalog's registration check exactly.
11. Confirmed i18n/types.ts's staff block has exactly the 11 keys the spec lists (notAuthorized, usageNoArgs, eventNotFound, userNotFound, alreadyAssigned, notAssigned, addSuccessPrefix, removeSuccessPrefix, notificationFailedNote, assignmentNotificationBody, removalNotificationBody) and checkin block has exactly the 4 keys listed (usageNoId, notFound, notAuthorized, authorizedStub); both en.ts and ru.ts define matching key sets. AC-catalog's own prose has a self-contradictory '9 keys:' lead-in immediately followed by an 11-item list and a correct '11 keys total' -- a wording typo, not a factual error (the list and count it tells TEST-RUNNER to verify are both correct, and the case explicitly instructs 'recount from the live file rather than trusting this list', so the check remains mechanical and unambiguous). Noted as a MINOR wording defect, not gate-failing since the actual pass condition is unaffected and requires no judgment call to execute.
12. Boundary conditions genuinely tested: AC1 constructs a REAL cross-event event_staff row and asserts refusal on event 2 / authorization on event 1 via live getEventStaffRow SQL, not just the pure predicate. AC3 constructs a REAL Postgres timestamptz ends_at 1 hour in the past and asserts refusal via a live handler dispatch, not just the pure isFinished unit test. AC7 explicitly separates AC7a (no-user, no users row at all) from AC7b (not-staff-for-event, a real user row with no event_staff row) as two distinct fixtures/dispatches -- the unstaffed-user vs no-user-row-at-all distinction is genuinely two separate live cases, not conflated.
13. Every dispatch case uses bot.handleUpdate() against a real grammy.Bot with a real command matcher and a stubbed outbound-API transformer only (bot.api.config.use) -- never a mocked/stubbed Context object. Confirmed by reading the harness script in the spec's Shared Setup section; this matches REQ-013/014/015/016/017's established convention and avoids the REQ-013 mocked-Context defect class.
14. -t filter strings checked against the real test files: eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts's actual it() titles contain 'AC1's negative case: ...', 'refuses with event-ended when...', 'exactly at endsAt is still allowed (isFinished is strictly-after)', and a 'buildCheckinRefusalAudit' describe block wrapping 4 it() cases -- every -t filter string in the spec (AC1/AC3/AC7's unit re-runs) is a genuine substring of an existing test's full name and will select the intended case(s) without ambiguity.

No check failed. Routing to TEST-RUNNER for Step 4.

issues.description: AC-catalog section's lead-in sentence says 'staff block (9 keys: ...)' immediately before listing and counting 11 keys ('... — 11 keys total'). The list and the '11 keys total' are both correct against the live apps/bot/src/i18n/types.ts; only the leading '9' is a stray typo. Does not block the gate because the case already instructs the runner to recount from the live file rather than trust the written list/count, so execution remains mechanical. Flagged for TEST-DESIGNER to fix the stray '9' on the next touch of this file, at the source per core-directives.md.
